d: Outside the castle. A tavern with a pergola. Spaldi in the bottom and the sea. It is evening. Flashes, thunders, hurricane. Jago, Roderigo, Cassio, Montano, later Otello. Cypriots and Venetian soldiers.
Othello, Jago, Cassio, Montano, People, Soldiers; later Desdemona.
An earthly room in the castle. Two large veronas on the sides: a door in the middle overlooking the garden. Jago on this side of the verona. Cassio on the other side.

After the choir is finished, Desdemona kisses the head of some of the Children, and some women kiss her the edge of her robe, and she puts a bag to the Navy. The choir moves away: Desdemona, followed by Emilia, enters the hall and moves towards Otello.
The great hall of the castle. On the right a vast peristyle with columns. This peristyle is annexed to a room of smaller proportions; at the bottom of the hall a veron. Othello, Jago, the Herald.
Othello, Lodovico, Roderigo, the Herald. Dignitarians of the Venetian Republic. Gentiluomini and Dame. Soldiers. Trombettieri from the bottom, then Jago with Desdemona and Emilia from the left.
Cassius followed by the Herald and said.

Desdemona's bedroom. Bed, kneeling, table, mirror, chairs. A burning lamp hung in front of the image of Our Lady standing above the kneeling room. It leads to the right. It is night. A light lit on the table. Desdemona and Emilia.
Othello, Emilia, Lodovico, Cassio and Jago. Then Montano with armed people.
